title: Multi-cluster registry
description: Named clusters with independent auth configs. Register/deregister clusters at runtime, per-cluster client caching, routing by cluster name. Orchestrates the auth methods and client pool across many clusters.

title: Informers scoped to managed resources
description: Watch streams scoped to resources Synchrotron has applied (not full cluster state), to reduce API server load. Integrates with health probes for restart-on-reconnect. Feeds live state into the reconciliation engine (downstream).

title: Cluster health probes & auto-reconnect
description: Periodic /healthz probes per cluster, exponential backoff on failure, automatic reconnection, surfaces cluster status for the API/UI. Supplies the up/down signal informers need for lifecycle decisions.

title: Exec-based credential plugin
description: Support kubeconfig exec plugins (aws-iam-authenticator, gke-gcloud-auth-plugin, etc.) — subprocess invocation per kubeconfig ExecConfig spec, response parsing, token caching respecting the plugin's expiration.

title: OIDC token refresh
description: OIDC authentication with refresh token flow. Handles expiry-driven refresh, caches current token, supports the common OIDC-provider-in-kubeconfig pattern.

title: In-cluster ServiceAccount auth
description: Support in-cluster auth via projected SA token (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/). Token rotation handling. Used when Synchrotron runs inside a Kubernetes cluster managing itself or another cluster.

title: Multi-repo orchestration
description: Repo registry: register/deregister repos at runtime, bounded concurrent fetches, per-repo state tracking, surface aggregate status. Coordinates the polling scheduler and workspace layer across many repos.

title: Webhook-triggered immediate fetch (consumer side)
description: Expose a trigger API on the git sync layer that the webhook & event system (h48.6) can call to force an immediate fetch for a given repo, bypassing the polling interval. Includes de-duplication so a burst of webhooks collapses into one fetch.

title: Git polling scheduler with jitter
description: Per-repo polling loop: configurable interval (default 3 min), random jitter to avoid thundering herd, pause/resume, graceful shutdown. Triggers fetch + HEAD comparison; does not handle the reconciliation reaction (that's the reconciliation engine's job).

title: Git GitHub App token authentication
description: GitHub App installation token auth: JWT signing with app private key, installation token exchange, token refresh before expiry. Needed for fine-grained per-repo permissions in GitHub-centric deployments.

title: Git SSH key authentication
description: Add SSH key auth support to the git client (password-protected keys, ssh-agent integration, known_hosts handling). Plugs into the credential abstraction established by the foundation sub-issue.

title: Kube client & kubeconfig auth + HTTP/2 pool
description: Foundation for cluster connector. Set up kube-rs (or similar) client with kubeconfig-based auth and a bounded HTTP/2 connection pool per cluster. Expose a typed client handle that other sub-issues (SA auth, OIDC, exec plugin, health probes, informers, multi-cluster) plug into. Crate: synchrotron-kube.
notes: Bounded pool sizing deferred to synchrotron-cd-h48.8.8 — kube-rs defaults are used. All auth/context/connectivity bits in scope are implemented.

title: Git core ops & workspace (HTTP basic auth)
description: Foundation for git sync. Implement the pure git client layer: shallow clone (depth=1), fetch updates, HEAD commit hash comparison against SQLite last-synced state, and workspace layout (bare repo cache + worktree per sync). HTTP basic auth only — SSH and GitHub App tokens are separate sub-issues. This is the MVP slice all other h48.1 sub-issues build on. Crate: synchrotron-git.
notes: libgit2 local transport does not support shallow fetch (git2 error -39). Production HTTPS/SSH clones work with depth=1 as designed; tests use with_depth(None) against local path fixtures. Exposed as Repo::depth: Option<i32> (default Some(1)).

title: Application Model & CRDs
description: Define Application and ApplicationSet CRDs. Application: source (repoURL, path, targetRevision, plugin), destination (cluster, namespace), syncPolicy (automated with selfHeal/prune/selfHealInterval, drift config with autoIgnore and manual ignore rules, sync waves), healthChecks (CEL overrides). ApplicationSet: generator trait/plugin system with v1 generators (git directories, cluster selector). Architecture designed for future generators (matrix, PR, SCM provider) as additive trait impls. Bootstrap config file (synchrotron.yaml) with same schema. AppProject for future RBAC.
close_reason: Implemented: 4-crate workspace, SQLite storage with schema+migrations+CRUD+tests, Application model types

title: Health Assessment Engine
description: Three-tier health assessment, no Lua. Tier 1: Built-in Rust functions for standard k8s types (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, Pod, Service, Ingress, PVC, CRD, HPA) - just read status fields. Tier 2: Condition convention - auto-detect status.conditions with type=Ready or Available, covers most operators/CRDs with zero config. Tier 3: CEL expression overrides per resource type for anything Tiers 1-2 don't cover. Aggregate app health = worst resource status. Statuses: Healthy, Progressing, Degraded, Suspended, Missing, Unknown. Readiness gates for sync waves. See DESIGN.md D6.

title: SQLite State Storage
description: Foundation layer. Schema for applications, sync history, resource state snapshots, health status, cache metadata. WAL mode for concurrent readers + single writer. Embedded migrations versioned with binary. Periodic compaction with configurable retention (default 30 days). Use rusqlite with bundled SQLite.
close_reason: Implemented: 4-crate workspace, SQLite storage with schema+migrations+CRUD+tests, Application model types

title: CLI & REST API
description: REST API (JSON over HTTP) as primary interface. Endpoints: apps CRUD + sync/diff/rollback/history, clusters CRUD, repos CRUD, system health. SSE streaming for live status watch. CLI (synchrotron) as thin HTTP client wrapping REST API. OpenAPI spec generated from code. Built on axum + serde_json. No gRPC - simplicity and curl-debuggability over wire efficiency. See DESIGN.md D7.

title: Smart Diff Engine
description: Critical differentiator. Four-layer drift detection: (1) Server-side dry-run normalization - apply with --dry-run=server to get normalized manifests, diff those vs live state. Handles defaulting, mutating webhooks, normalization automatically. (2) Auto controller-aware ignore - discover HPAs/VPAs/KEDA ScaledObjects, resolve targets, auto-ignore managed fields (spec.replicas for HPA, resources for VPA). Cache controller mapping, refresh every 5 min. All auto-ignore on by default. (3) User-defined ignore rules via jsonPointers, managedFieldsManagers, jmesPathExpressions. (4) Server-side apply field ownership - only diff fields Synchrotron owns via fieldManager. See DESIGN.md D4 for full spec.

title: Cluster Connector & Auth
description: Auth methods: kubeconfig, in-cluster SA, OIDC token refresh, exec-based credential plugins. HTTP/2 connection pooling per cluster with bounded pool size. Periodic /healthz probes and auto-reconnect. Informers (watch streams) for managed resources only. Multi-cluster: named clusters with independent auth.

title: RocksDB State Storage
close_reason: Replaced RocksDB with SQLite per D1 revision

title: Webhook & Event System
description: Inbound webhooks: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket push events with HMAC signature verification. Internal event bus (async channels) for decoupling producers/consumers. De-duplication and coalescing. Outbound notifications (webhook/callback) on sync success/failure. System works fine without webhooks (polling-only is fully supported).

title: Deployment Orchestrator
description: Server-side apply with Synchrotron as field manager. Pruning (opt-in) for removed resources. Sync waves and hooks (pre-sync, post-sync, sync-fail). Rollback support tracking last N successful syncs. Resource ordering (Namespace -> RBAC -> Deployment -> Service).

title: Reconciliation Engine
description: Core reconciliation loop: event-driven (webhook/poll triggers) + periodic auto-heal (default 3 min). Per-app: fetch desired from cache, fetch live from informer cache, run smart diff, enqueue sync if drift. Parallel app processing with bounded worker pool. Debouncing for rapid-fire events. Sync wave support.

title: Plugin System (Local + Sidecar)
description: Plugin system for manifest rendering. Local plugins: JSON-RPC over stdio (subprocess). Sidecar plugins: gRPC to containers. Built-in support for raw YAML directories. Ship Helm and Kustomize as local plugins. Plugin output cached by input hash.

title: Manifest Cache (LRU)
description: LRU manifest cache keyed by (app, commit-hash, params-hash). Configurable max memory (default 350MB). Invalidation on new commits. Startup warm-up from SQLite for recently-active apps. Hit/miss metrics.

title: Git Synchronization Engine
description: Implement git sync engine: shallow clones, change detection via commit hash comparison, multi-repo support, credential management (SSH/HTTP/GitHub App tokens), configurable polling with jitter, webhook-triggered immediate fetch. Workspace management with bare repos + worktrees.

title: Design Documentation & Architectural Decisions
description: Create and maintain DESIGN.md with key architectural decisions, technology choices, and design rationale

title: Operational Simplicity & UX
description: Design simple deployment, configuration, and operational workflows. Includes: single-binary installation (+ CRDs via Helm chart), configuration management, Prometheus metrics and structured logging, multi-cluster deployment patterns, upgrade/migration strategies.

title: Performance & Scalability Optimization
description: Ensure system meets performance targets: <5s webhook-to-sync latency, 10,000+ apps per instance, <50KB memory per app baseline, 50+ clusters per instance. Includes benchmarking harness, profiling, optimization passes, and load testing.

title: Core Architecture & Design Goals
description: Establish the architectural foundation for Synchrotron-CD, a lightweight GitOps alternative to Argo CD

title: Bounded HTTP/2 pool sizing per cluster
description: Wire max_idle_per_host (and related hyper pool knobs) through ClusterConfig into the kube client. Currently KubeClient uses kube-rs defaults via Client::try_from(config). To bound the pool we need to construct a hyper_util Client with builder().pool_max_idle_per_host(n), layer kube::client::ConfigExt service layers on it, then Client::new(service, ns). Deferred from h48.8.1 because it's additive to working code and not on the critical path for downstream sub-issues.
